messages:
anna: Quick heads-up — I'm planning a Terraform module change for GPU fleet sharding and AZ scheduling. Goal: let a logical GPU pool be split into N shards and express AZ preference without creating a bunch of little pools. Opening an RFC PR tomorrow. Need eyes on migration, IAM/KMS impacts, and CI gating.

mike: SGTM in principle. Two quick concerns: how this affects reserved/dedicated capacity naming, and whether node pool resource addresses change (we can't break existing IG names).

anna: Good call. Plan is to ship as a v2 major release but keep resource addresses unchanged. We'll accept old var names via a compatibility shim and mark them deprecated. No renames of managed instance groups.

sarah: For GitOps — we should do a staged rollout. Changing affinity or labels can cause node replacements. Do we want a canary cluster first?

anna: Yes. Two-phase rollout: 1) publish v2 module that only adds new inputs and defaults (no resource diffs), 2) update specific clusters to opt-in to sharding, 3) ramp with canary namespaces and roll window. CI will require manual approval for the first few clusters.

raj: Heads up on KMS: v2 will support multi-region CMKs via alias ARNs. That implies cross-account iam:Decrypt allowances in some regions and we must not auto-rotate CMKs during rollout. Also call out least-privilege in the docs.

mike: Quotas — if customers increase shard_count we'll create more node pools in parallel. We need to request GPU quota bumps in target regions ahead of time. Remember the eu-west-1 outage last quarter.

devops-bot: lint: terraform fmt OK. tfsec: 2 warnings — KMS key policy uses wildcard.

anna: Proposed variables snippet (will be in PR):
```
variable "shard_count" {
  type        = number
  default     = 1
  description = "Number of shards to split a logical GPU pool into (1 = no sharding)"
}
variable "az_preference" {
  type        = list(string)
  default     = ["eu-west-1a", "eu-west-1b"]
  description = "Preferred AZ ordering for shard placement; module will prefer these AZs where quotas exist"
}
```

mike: Add a 'max_drain_time' input too so rolling replacements don't violate SLOs. Also add lifecycle { ignore_changes = [metadata] } for things we don't want GitOps to constantly reconcile.

sarah: CI idea: require `terraform plan -out=plan.binary` artifact and a safety check job that diffs resource addresses against a whitelist. If any managed instance group names would rename, fail the pipeline.

anna: Agreed. Also adding a migration helper script (in tools/) that can run `terraform state mv` for teams that want to consolidate existing pools into shards. We will not perform automatic state moves in the GitOps apply — manual migration only.

raj: About the module versioning — are we all OK with v2.0? That signals breaking changes even though we try to be non-destructive. v2 lets us document migration steps clearly. We'll need an upgrade guide and a KMS/IAM checklist for security owners.

mike: +1 for v2. Also ask product for a cost note: more shards can increase temporary node spin-ups. Estimate: ~+15% infra cost at shard_count=2 for p4d-like workloads under our profiling.

sarah: I'll add a staging canary to the GitOps pipeline this week and run a dry-run apply against a copy of state (testing backend) to confirm no address changes.

anna: CI gating plan: require two approvals for first 3 clusters, then auto-approve for the rest once canary passes. Add automated rollback step: if more than X% of nodes in a cluster fail health checks within Y minutes, trigger revert to previous module version.

devops-bot: Ticket INFRA-1423 created for regional quota requests (eu-west-1,p-asia-south1).

mike: Also include an ops playbook for emergency rollback: 1) pin module to previous version in repo, 2) `gitops-controller` will pick up and apply, 3) monitor node health and drain metrics. Keep the plan artifact handy.

anna: I'll add cost delta and rollback runbook to the PR. Anything else?

raj: Add a test scenario for KMS key rotation failure — simulate denied decrypts and ensure the apply fails cleanly with clear logs so we can rollback.

sarah: I'll mock a canary apply and share plan diff later today.

anna: Thanks everyone — I'll tag you on the PR when it's up. Will include deprecation notes for old inputs, migration helper, CI gating, cost estimates, and the KMS/IAM checklist. :rocket:
